name: Module private authorization belongs only to one composition edge revision

input.source_text: module M { public fun reach() -> Object { try { secret() } catch e { e } } } class Granted mixin M private { private fun secret() -> Symbol { :g } } class Other mixin M { private fun secret() -> Symbol { :o } } class Revoked mixin M private { private fun secret() -> Symbol { :r } } module Q { public fun run() -> Object { let granted = Granted.new().reach(); let other = Other.new().reach(); let before = Revoked.new().reach(); let removed = Reflection::Class.remove_module(Revoked, :M); let added = Revoked.add_module(:M); [granted, other, before, Revoked.new().reach()] } } Q.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C057 scopes Module private authorization to (host logical Class, closed Module identity, composition edge, edge revision), and all four halves hold. The earlier reason measured the wrong shape: it read a private method on the MODULE, but the grant lets the Module's code reach the HOST's private selector, so a Module-internal call was always allowed and proved nothing. Measured correctly, a granted edge reaches the host's private selector while another host composing the same Module is denied, removing the edge revokes the authorization, and re-including without private authorization does not inherit the old grant. `module_has_private_access` reads the ACTIVE revision's edges, which is what makes removal atomic and re-inclusion a fresh edge.
